clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: An adult arrives at an outpatient clinic with fever, cough, conjunctivitis, and a new rash that began on the face and is spreading downward. The RN suspects measles, and an airborne infection isolation room is available. Which action is most appropriate?

options.A: Place the client in a private room with the door closed and use droplet precautions while awaiting laboratory confirmation of measles.
options.B: Place a mask on the client, move the client promptly to an airborne infection isolation room, and use a fit-tested N95 respirator for care.
options.C: Use contact precautions in a private room and add an N95 respirator if the client develops worsening cough or respiratory distress.
options.D: Keep the client separated in the waiting area while arranging laboratory testing, then begin airborne isolation if measles is confirmed.

semantic_correction.rationale: Current CDC measles infection-control guidance instructs healthcare settings to rapidly identify and isolate patients with known or suspected measles, provide source control, use Standard plus Airborne Precautions, immediately place the patient in an airborne infection isolation room when available, and have healthcare personnel entering the room use respiratory protection at least as protective as a fit-tested NIOSH-certified N95 respirator. The 2026 NCSBN NCLEX-RN Test Plan explicitly places airborne/droplet/contact transmission, isolation, infection-prevention principles, and staff/client infection-prevention education within Safety and Infection Prevention and Control. B is therefore the uniquely best action. A uses droplet rather than airborne precautions. C uses contact precautions and delays appropriate respiratory protection. D delays required isolation until laboratory confirmation even though CDC guidance applies to suspected measles. Therefore B is correct.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: For suspected measles in a healthcare setting, initiate Airborne Precautions immediately: provide source control, place the client promptly in an AIIR when available, and use appropriate respiratory protection rather than waiting for laboratory confirmation.

near_duplicate_check.note: V2-Q0676 tests an oxygen-related fire hazard. V2-Q0626 tests occupational needlestick response. V2-Q0271 tests hand hygiene after contact with patient surroundings/equipment. V2-Q0775 tests immediate Airborne Precautions and AIIR placement for suspected measles. Targeted repository search for measles/airborne-isolation content returned no matching item before staging.

option_audit.A: Plausible isolation action but uses droplet rather than required airborne precautions.
option_audit.B: Correct. It provides source control, prompt AIIR placement and appropriate respirator use without waiting for confirmation.
option_audit.C: Plausible PPE response but uses the wrong transmission category and delays respirator use based on symptom severity.
option_audit.D: Plausible diagnostic workflow but leaves the suspected measles client outside required airborne isolation while awaiting testing.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible best answer. The stem supplies a classic suspected-measles presentation and confirms an AIIR is available. Current CDC guidance applies Airborne Precautions to suspected measles immediately. B alone implements source control, AIIR placement and recommended respiratory protection without delay.
